_README: Authored English copy for the Tripwix partner homes, merged over the API payload by scripts/tripwix-import.mjs. The supplier's own text is byte-identical to their canonical pages on tripwix.com, so publishing it would make these 35 URLs duplicates of a site that already outranks us on those strings. Everything here is written from the structured data — amenities, layout, address, region — and never paraphrased from theirs. Keys are the supplier reference. Fields: name (only where theirs carries back-office noise), tagline, description (HTML), seoTitle, seoDescription, imageAlts (positional, index 0 = hero).

PT0023.tagline: A restored quinta on the Douro's edge, with its own vineyard and river dock
PT0023.description:
Casa do Rolapipas sits at the water's edge in the Douro Valley, on a bend of the river where the terraced vineyards climb the far bank in near-vertical lines. The house has its own dock, so the river is not a view you admire from a terrace — it is somewhere you push off from before breakfast.

Six bedrooms and seven bathrooms open onto the vineyard and the water, sleeping fourteen without anyone drawing the short straw. The pool sits between the house and the river, on a lawn that runs to the bank. Inside, an indoor fireplace anchors the living room for the cold, clear winters this valley is known for, and a wine cooler waits for whatever you carry back from the quintas upstream.

The kitchen is set up for people who intend to use it — dishwasher, oven, full cooking basics, dining table, wine glasses for a table of fourteen. If you would rather not, a chef can be arranged to cook in the house, and breakfast preparation and daily housekeeping are available on request.

This is Douro wine country at its most concentrated: port quintas within a short drive, river cruises from the local landings, and the terraced UNESCO landscape in every direction. The estate is gated, with parking on site, and the setting is quiet enough that the loudest thing most evenings is the water.

PT0277.tagline: A heritage house above the river, with a games room and a cellar's worth of wine storage
PT0277.description:
Casa de Caiz is an old Douro house that has been brought forward without being stripped of what made it worth keeping. Stone and timber remain; the river and mountain views were always the point, and they still are. Six bedrooms, six and a half bathrooms, ten guests.

The private pool sits in the garden with the valley falling away beyond it. There is a games room for the hours between lunch and dinner, an indoor fireplace for the evenings, and a wine cooler that will hold whatever the surrounding quintas persuade you to buy. A dedicated workspace means a longer stay does not have to be a holiday only.

The Douro rewards slowness. Port houses and vineyards sit within easy reach, the river runs below, and the roads here were built to follow the contours rather than beat them. The house is set up for a group that wants a base rather than a series of hotel rooms — one long table, one kitchen, one garden, and the valley doing the rest.

PT0273.tagline: A four-bedroom Douro house with a heated pool and a jacuzzi facing the valley
PT0273.description:
Quinta da Lameirinha is the smaller kind of Douro house — four bedrooms, eight guests — which makes it the one to take when the group is a family or two couples rather than a wedding party. What it does not scale down is the view: the valley opens out below the terrace and keeps going.

The pool is heated, which matters here more than people expect. The Douro is a spring and autumn destination as much as a summer one, and a heated pool with a jacuzzi beside it turns a cool October afternoon into the best part of the day. A gas fireplace handles the evenings indoors, and there is air conditioning for the valley's genuinely hot Julys.

Outside there is a lawn garden, a BBQ grill and a terrace positioned for the long light. The house sits close enough to the wine quintas for tastings to be an afternoon rather than an expedition, and far enough from anything to be quiet.

PT0186.tagline: A hilltop quinta with its own vineyard, a heated pool and wood fires
PT0186.description:
Quinta do Pinho stands on a hilltop with its own vineyard running below it, which is the arrangement most people picture when they imagine the Douro and rarely get. Six bedrooms and nine and a half bathrooms sleep fourteen, and the house is old enough to have a history and worked-on enough to be comfortable.

The pool is heated and positioned for the view rather than for shelter. Indoors there are wood-burning fireplaces — actual wood, with guards, not a gas approximation — which is the right way to spend a February evening at this altitude. Mountain views run in every direction the vineyard does not.

A hilltop position in the Douro means two things: the light, which arrives early and leaves late, and the quiet. Port quintas and river landings are within driving distance, and the UNESCO terraces that make this valley unlike anywhere else in Portugal start at the garden wall.

PT0148.tagline: A vineyard house at Casal de Loivos, with a wine cellar, spa and sauna
PT0148.description:
Quinta Vale das Papas sits at Casal de Loivos, which is the address people who know the Douro react to — the viewpoint there is the one on the postcards, and this house sits in that landscape rather than looking at it from elsewhere. Six bedrooms, twelve guests, the river below and vineyards on all sides.

The house is built for staying in. There is a wine cellar, a spa with a sauna and a jacuzzi, a games room with a billiards table, and an indoor fireplace for when the valley turns cold. The private pool faces the river. A laptop-friendly workspace means the longer stay this valley deserves is actually workable.

What Casal de Loivos gives you is elevation. The Douro from up here reads as a whole system — terraces, river, the quintas on the opposite bank — instead of the fragment you see from the road. Port houses and tastings are a short drive down; getting back up in time for sunset is the only scheduling that matters.

PT0259.tagline: Seven bedrooms above Alijó, with a spa, outdoor jacuzzi and wine cellar
PT0259.description:
Encostas da Baronesa is the Douro house to take when the group is genuinely large. Seven bedrooms, ten bathrooms, eighteen guests — and, unusually for that size, no sense that the last two bedrooms were an afterthought. It sits above Alijó with the river in the distance and the hills close.

The facilities are the reason to choose it over something smaller. There is a spa with a sauna, an outdoor jacuzzi positioned for the view, a gym, a games room with billiards, and a wine cellar. Two dedicated workspaces make it viable for a group mixing a holiday with something else. Indoors, a fireplace and generous living space keep eighteen people from feeling like a crowd.

Alijó is proper Douro — port country, terraced slopes, quintas that have been in the same families for generations. For a milestone birthday, a family reunion or a company retreat, the combination of scale and setting here is rare enough to be worth planning a trip around.

PT0198.tagline: A historic farmhouse with an indoor pool, for eighteen in the Douro hills
PT0198.description:
Quinta da Tojeira is a working farmhouse's worth of building — nine bedrooms, eighteen guests — reworked with a modern hand and, crucially, given an indoor pool. In a valley whose best months are shoulder-season, an indoor pool and a heated one outside change what the house is good for.

There is a spa with a sauna, an indoor jacuzzi, a games room with billiards, and an indoor fireplace. Mountain views run around the property. The scale suits a group that wants to take over somewhere completely: one long table, one kitchen, and enough separate space that eighteen people are not permanently in each other's way.

The Douro's historic farmhouses were built for the harvest, with thick walls and deep shade, and that inheritance is what keeps this house cool in August and solid in January. Port quintas, the river and the terraced UNESCO landscape are the reason to be here; the house is the reason to stay longer than you planned.

PT0068.tagline: Eight bedrooms on the riverbank, with a private dock and boat slip
PT0068.description:
Casa do Rio sits on the bank of the Douro at Quinta do Merouço, with a private dock and a boat slip — which puts it in a small category of Portuguese rental houses where arriving or leaving by water is a real option rather than a brochure line. Eight bedrooms, sixteen guests.

The pool and terrace face the river. Inside there is an indoor fireplace and the kind of living space a group of sixteen needs if the house is going to work over a week rather than a weekend. Beach essentials are provided for the river shore below.

The Douro here is wide and slow, and the far bank is terraced to the skyline. River cruises pass, port quintas sit within a short drive, and the landscape is the one UNESCO listed rather than a version of it seen from a distance. For a group that wants the river as the centre of the stay — swimming, boats, long afternoons on the bank — this is the address.

PT0253.tagline: A clifftop house above Praia da Salema, with a sauna, gym and heated pool
PT0253.description:
Villa Belvedere stands on the cliffs above Praia da Salema, on the stretch of the western Algarve that stayed low-rise while the centre of the coast did not. Five bedrooms, ten guests, and the Atlantic filling the view from almost everywhere in the house.

The house is unusually well equipped for its size. There is a sauna, an outdoor jacuzzi, a gym in the building, a heated pool, a piano and an indoor fireplace — the kind of list that usually belongs to a house twice as large. A dedicated workspace and a gated setting make longer stays practical.

Salema is still a fishing village, which in the western Algarve is no longer a given. The beach below is one of the good ones, the coastline west towards Sagres is protected parkland, and the restaurants are the sort that do not need to advertise. A chef can be arranged in the house if you would rather not go out at all.

PT0256.tagline: An oceanfront house in Estoril, with the beach at the door and a lift to every floor
PT0256.description:
Villa Laura is on the seafront at Estoril, which is a rarer thing than the Lisbon coast's reputation suggests — most of the grand houses here sit a street or two back. This one has beach access and beachfront position, eight bedrooms, and a lift serving the floors, which matters in a house this tall.

The private pool sits above the ocean. There is a gym in the building, and the layout suits a group of twelve who want to be within walking distance of restaurants and the train rather than driving everywhere.

Estoril is fifteen minutes from Cascais and half an hour from central Lisbon by the coastal line, which runs along the water the whole way. The casino, the beaches and the old resort architecture are on the doorstep; Sintra is a short drive inland. For a group that wants the sea and the city in the same trip without choosing, this is the position.

PT0237.tagline: A five-bedroom Comporta house with a heated pool, set back in the pines
PT0237.description:
PT-A-Sud sits off the Estrada das Bicas in the pine country behind Comporta, which is where the good houses here have always been — close enough to the beach to walk it in the evening, far enough back to keep the silence. Five bedrooms, twelve guests.

The pool is heated and private, in a garden that has been left to look like the landscape rather than fight it. Inside there is an indoor fireplace for the surprisingly cold Atlantic evenings, a wine cooler, air conditioning for August, and a laptop-friendly workspace for the stays that run longer than a week.

Comporta's appeal is specific and easy to miss if you arrive expecting the Algarve. The beaches are wide, empty and cold; the villages are low, white and quiet; the rice fields and the pine forest do the rest. Lisbon is a little over an hour away, which is close enough for a day and far enough that nobody does it twice.

PT0248.tagline: A gated contemporary retreat at Carvalhal, minutes from the Comporta beaches
PT0248.description:
Casa na Areia sits in a gated development at Carvalhal, on the stretch of coast between Comporta and Melides where the sand runs for kilometres with almost nothing built on it. Four bedrooms, seven bathrooms, twelve guests — a generous bathroom count for the size, which tells you how the house is meant to be used.

The pool is heated and private, and the architecture is the low, pale, horizontal kind that Comporta has made its own. An indoor fireplace handles the evenings; a BBQ grill handles most of the dinners.

Carvalhal's beaches are the reason to be here — Praia do Carvalhal and Praia do Pego are a short drive, both wide and both quiet outside August. The beach restaurants along this coast are among the best in Portugal and none of them look like it. Being gated means the house is easy to leave and easy to come back to.

PT0175.tagline: A contemporary Comporta house with its own tennis court, deep in the pines
PT0175.description:
Alma da Comporta is set among the pines with a private tennis court, which in this part of the coast is unusual — most houses here choose the pool and stop. Five bedrooms, ten guests, and an architecture that keeps to the horizontal lines Comporta is known for.

The private pool sits on a terrace facing the trees. Indoors there is a fireplace, and the living space is arranged around the outside rather than away from it. The seven-night minimum is a fair reflection of what the house is for: this is not a weekend address.

Comporta rewards the longer stay. The beaches take a while to learn, the rice fields change with the light, and the restaurants are spread out enough that eating well takes planning. Between the tennis court, the pool and the pines, the house holds a group of ten for a week without anyone needing to leave.

PT0071.tagline: A three-bedroom cabana with resort facilities — gym, spa, beach club and golf
PT0071.description:
The 3Br Cabana Villa is the smallest house in this collection and, in one specific way, the most useful: it comes with resort facilities attached. A gym, a spa, a community sauna, a beach club, bikes and golf are all available to guests, which is not something a standalone Comporta house can offer.

Three bedrooms, six guests, a private pool and an indoor fireplace. The rustic-luxury register here is the Comporta one — natural materials, low ceilings, nothing shiny.

For a couple or a small family who want the Comporta landscape without taking on a large house, this is the sensible answer. The one-night minimum makes it viable for a short stay, which almost nothing else in the area allows, and the beach club solves the question of what to do with a wet afternoon.

PT0014.tagline: A beach house at Brejos da Carregueira, built for long Comporta summers
PT0014.description:
Vale da Raposa sits at Brejos da Carregueira de Baixo, in the cluster of small settlements behind the Comporta dunes where the houses are low and the roads are sand for the last stretch. Five bedrooms, twelve guests, a private pool and an indoor fireplace.

The house is detailed in the way the good Comporta houses are — thatch, lime, timber, and very little that draws attention to itself. The pool and terrace face the garden; the beach is a short drive.

This part of the Alentejo coast has a particular rhythm. Mornings are for the beach before the wind picks up, afternoons for the shade, evenings for a long table outdoors. The house is built around that assumption, and a group of twelve settles into it quickly.

PT0232.tagline: A minimalist house on the Praia do Pego road, with bikes and a heated pool
PT0232.description:
Casa da Palicada sits on the Alameda da Praia do Pego, which is the road to one of the two beaches that made Comporta's reputation. Four bedrooms, eight guests, and an interior stripped back to the point where the light does most of the work.

The pool is heated. There are bikes, which on this flat, sandy, pine-shaded stretch of coast is the correct way to reach the beach. An indoor fireplace and a BBQ grill cover the two ends of a Comporta day.

Praia do Pego is wide, Atlantic and usually near-empty outside high summer. The beach restaurants here are the ones people drive from Lisbon for. A seven-night minimum suits the house: it is designed for a week of doing very little, extremely well.

PT0053.name: Villa Arroz
PT0053.tagline: A Possanco house among the rice fields, with a heated pool and a long terrace
PT0053.description:
Villa Arroz is at Possanco, on the Rua das Palmeiras, in the flat country where the Sado rice fields meet the pine forest. The name is not decorative — this is rice-growing land, and the fields shift colour through the season in a way that becomes the view.

Six bedrooms, twelve guests, a heated private pool and a terrace built long enough for a table that seats everyone. The register is the Comporta one: low, white, unhurried.

Possanco sits between Comporta village and the Carvalhal beaches, which puts both within a short drive and neither on top of you. Storks nest on the poles across the rice fields, the light in the late afternoon is the reason photographers come here, and the seven-night minimum is the house telling you what it is for.

PT0145.tagline: An ocean-view house at Afeiteira, with a heated pool and the beach close
PT0145.description:
4 Serras sits at Afeiteira de Baixo with an ocean view, which on this coast is less common than the beach-adjacent addresses suggest — most Comporta houses sit behind the dunes with no sight of the water at all. Five bedrooms, twelve guests.

The pool is heated and private, the terrace faces the sea, and an indoor fireplace covers the evenings when the Atlantic wind arrives. Beach essentials are provided, which saves the first-morning trip into town.

The Alentejo coast between Comporta and Melides is one of the emptiest developed coastlines in southern Europe — long sand, cold clean water, and almost no buildings above two storeys. The house is set up for a group that intends to use the beach daily and eat at home most nights.

PT0009.tagline: A hillside villa above Albufeira, with heated pools and a private tennis court
PT0009.description:
Mirante 1 sits on the hillside above Albufeira with an ocean view, heated pools and a tennis court — a combination that puts it in a different category from the town below. Six bedrooms, seven and a half bathrooms, twelve guests.

The grounds do most of the work: lawn garden, private outdoor pool, tennis court, and a BBQ terrace positioned for the sunset. Indoors there is a billiards table, a games collection and air conditioning that earns its keep in an Algarve July.

Albufeira divides opinion, and the answer is usually altitude. From up here you get the beaches, the marina and the restaurants within a ten-minute drive, and none of the noise. Olhos de Água and Praia da Falésia are close, and the seven-night minimum suits a family taking the whole week.

PT0223.tagline: A Quinta do Lago-area villa with indoor and outdoor pools, sauna and gym
PT0223.description:
Encosta do Lago 5 sits in the Encosta do Lago development at Almancil, immediately alongside the Quinta do Lago estate — the golf and lagoon country that has anchored the central Algarve's reputation for forty years. Six bedrooms, twelve guests.

The draw is that there are two pools: one outside on the terrace, one indoors, which makes the house work in February as well as July. There is a sauna, a gym, a fitness and spa area, and an indoor fireplace. A five-night minimum keeps it to proper stays.

Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo golf courses are minutes away, as is the Ria Formosa lagoon and the long beach beyond it. Almancil itself has the concentration of good restaurants that the resorts around it do not. For a golfing group or a family splitting between courses and beach, the position is close to ideal.

PT0276.tagline: A modern Tavira villa with ocean views, a heated pool and a lift
PT0276.description:
Perogil 58 sits in the Quinta do Perogil development on the edge of Tavira, in the eastern Algarve — the quieter half of the coast, where the Ria Formosa islands sit offshore and the towns kept their shape. Four bedrooms, six bathrooms, eight guests.

The pool is heated and the terrace looks towards the ocean. There is a lift in the building, which makes the upper floors and the roof terrace usable for everyone rather than the agile. A BBQ grill covers most evenings.

Tavira is the eastern Algarve's best town — a Roman bridge, a river, tiled churches and a working fishing fleet, none of it arranged for visitors. The island beaches are reached by ferry, which keeps them empty, and Spain is forty minutes east. It is the part of the coast people move to after holidaying in the other part.

PT0164.tagline: An Albufeira villa with a glass-walled infinity pool and a wine cellar
PT0164.description:
Villa Mare is built around a glass-walled infinity pool — the kind where the water meets a vertical pane and the ocean sits behind it — which is the feature the house is known for and the reason to choose it. Five bedrooms, ten guests, above Albufeira at Cerro da Águia.

Beyond the pool there is a wine cellar, a wine cooler, a gym, a games room with billiards and a heated pool. The ocean view runs the length of the terrace.

Cerro da Águia puts you above Albufeira and Olhos de Água with the beaches a few minutes down. Praia da Falésia — the long red-cliff beach that most people picture when they picture the Algarve — is close. The house is set up for a group that wants a striking place to come back to rather than somewhere merely comfortable.

PT0283.tagline: An oceanfront mansion at Porches, with a lift, sauna and heated pool
PT0283.description:
Diamante Azul stands on the ocean at Porches, on the stretch of central Algarve cliff between Armação de Pêra and Carvoeiro where the rock is gold and the water drops away straight from the terrace. Eight bedrooms and twelve and a half bathrooms across a house built at genuine mansion scale.

There is a lift serving the floors, a sauna, a gym in the building, a jacuzzi, a gas fireplace and a heated pool. Beach and ocean views run along the seaward side.

Porches sits in the middle of the Algarve's best coastline. Benagil and its sea cave are minutes west, Praia da Marinha — regularly named among Europe's finest beaches — is a short drive, and Carvoeiro's restaurants are close enough for dinner without a plan. For a group that wants the coast at its most dramatic and a house to match, this is the address.

PT0099.tagline: An eight-bedroom garden villa near Quinta do Lago, with a heated pool and spa
PT0099.description:
Granvila is a large, green, low-slung house in the Quinta do Lago area of the central Algarve, built around its garden rather than looking out over a view. Eight bedrooms, nine bathrooms, sixteen guests — one of the biggest houses in this collection.

The pool is heated and private, set in mature planting that gives the place its oasis quality. There is a spa, an indoor fireplace, and two workspaces for groups mixing work with a longer stay. The seven-night minimum matches the scale.

The position is the central Algarve's most convenient: Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo golf within minutes, Almancil's restaurants close, Faro airport twenty minutes away, and the Ria Formosa beaches beyond the lagoon. For a large family group or two families travelling together, sixteen beds this well distributed are hard to find here.

PT0084.tagline: A four-hectare private estate at Vale Currais, with a tennis court and in-house chef
PT0084.description:
Vilarabe is an estate rather than a villa — four hectares of private land at Vale Currais in the central Algarve, with a tennis court, a gym, ocean views and a house at the centre of it. Six bedrooms, twelve guests.

An in-house chef is available, which given the scale of the grounds is the sensible way to eat: there is a wine cooler, a piano, an indoor fireplace and a terrace that runs the length of the house. The pool is heated and private, and the land around it means no neighbours in any direction.

Four hectares in the central Algarve is close to unheard of. It buys total privacy within twenty minutes of the coast's best beaches — Marinha, Benagil, Carvoeiro — and makes the house viable for a wedding, a milestone birthday or a family that simply does not want to see anyone for a week.

PT0021.tagline: A contemporary oceanfront house at Porches, with a wine cellar and long terrace
PT0021.description:
Casa da Rocha sits at Aldeamento do Levante in Porches, facing the ocean straight on. Five bedrooms, ten guests, and an architecture that keeps the sea in view from almost every room rather than saving it for one terrace.

There is a wine cellar, a private outdoor pool, a long terrace and two workspaces. The finish is contemporary and restrained — glass, pale stone, and very little competing with the water.

This is the best-looking stretch of the Algarve coast. Praia da Marinha, Benagil and the Seven Hanging Valleys trail are within a short drive, Carvoeiro and Ferragudo cover dinner, and the cliffs here turn gold in the late afternoon in a way that explains why this coast gets photographed as much as it does.

PT0141.tagline: A Quinta do Lago villa with indoor and outdoor pools, facing the golf
PT0141.description:
Villa 19 Monte Golf sits within Quinta do Lago itself, on the Monte Golf development, with a golf course view from the terrace. Eight bedrooms and eleven bathrooms make it the largest house in the collection's Algarve group, sleeping sixteen.

There are two pools — one heated outdoors, one indoors — plus a jacuzzi, a gym, a games room and an indoor fireplace. For a golfing group this is close to the ideal arrangement: the course outside, and everything needed for the hours off it inside.

Quinta do Lago is the central Algarve's most established address, and the reasons hold up: three championship courses, the Ria Formosa nature reserve, the beach at Praia do Ancão reached by the wooden bridge, and a concentration of good restaurants at Almancil. The seven-night minimum is standard for the estate.

PT0018.tagline: A clifftop villa with an outdoor jacuzzi and heated pool, central Algarve
PT0018.description:
Villa Trevo stands on a clifftop in the central Algarve with the ocean directly below. Five bedrooms, twelve guests, in a gated setting with a heated pool and an outdoor jacuzzi positioned for the sunset.

There is a fitness and spa area, a community sauna, an indoor fireplace and a terrace built along the seaward side. The house is finished at the level its position demands — this is the most expensive property in the collection, and the clifftop is why.

The central Algarve cliffs between Carvoeiro and Armação de Pêra are the coast at its most dramatic: sea caves, hidden coves reached by steps, and the Seven Hanging Valleys walk running along the top. Praia da Marinha and Benagil are close, and the drive to Faro airport is under an hour.

PT0131.tagline: An eight-bedroom house on the Sintra coast, with a tennis court and ocean views
PT0131.description:
Beachfront Sintra sits on the Estrada do Rodízio at Colares, on the Atlantic edge of the Sintra-Cascais natural park. Eight bedrooms and sixteen guests make it the largest house on this part of the coast, and the tennis court and private pool give a group that size somewhere to go.

The ocean view runs across the front, and there is an indoor fireplace for the evenings — necessary here, where the Atlantic wind arrives most afternoons regardless of season.

This coast is a different Portugal from the Algarve: cold, powerful surf beaches at Praia Grande and Praia das Maçãs, cliffs at Cabo da Roca, and the Sintra hills with their palaces fifteen minutes inland. Lisbon is forty minutes. The seven-night minimum suits a house designed for a group taking the whole week.

PT0169.tagline: A secluded Sintra house with a heated pool and a sauna, in the hills
PT0169.description:
Casa de Cima sits at Largo de Santo António in Sintra, set back into the hillside with the wooded slopes rising behind it. Five bedrooms, ten guests, and the seclusion that gives the house its name.

The pool is heated — which on this side of the Serra, where the sea mist sits into the morning, is not optional — and there is a sauna, an indoor fireplace and a workspace. The garden and BBQ terrace face the hillside view.

Sintra is a UNESCO landscape and behaves like one: the Pena Palace, the Moorish castle, Quinta da Regaleira and Monserrate are all within a few kilometres, and the microclimate keeps the hills green when the rest of the country is not. The Atlantic beaches at Praia Grande are ten minutes down, and Lisbon is under an hour. A seven-night minimum matches how long it takes to see any of it properly.

PT0269.tagline: A Cascais house on the golf, with ocean views and wood fires
PT0269.description:
Fairview Villa is on the Rua do Golfe at Quinta da Marinha, Cascais, facing the golf course with the Atlantic beyond it. Six bedrooms, fourteen guests, and a wood-burning fireplace that gets used more than visitors expect on this exposed stretch of coast.

The house has a golf course view and an ocean view, a BBQ terrace and a laptop-friendly workspace. The four-night minimum makes it one of the more flexible houses here for a long weekend.

Quinta da Marinha sits between Cascais town and Guincho beach, inside the Sintra-Cascais natural park. The golf is at the door, the Guincho surf and kitesurf beaches are five minutes west, Cascais marina and old town are five minutes east, and central Lisbon is forty minutes by the coastal road or the train.

PT0076.tagline: A Guincho house above the surf coast, with a heated pool and games room
PT0076.description:
Villa Guincho sits on the Rua da Portela do Pão above Guincho, the exposed Atlantic beach west of Cascais where the wind reliably arrives and the kitesurfers arrive with it. Six bedrooms, sixteen guests, and an ocean view across the dunes to the water.

The pool is heated, which on this coast is the difference between using it and looking at it. There is a games room with billiards, a fireplace, two workspaces, golf nearby and a terrace angled away from the prevailing wind.

Guincho is inside the Sintra-Cascais natural park, so the dunes and the pine behind them are protected and the coastline stays as it is. Cabo da Roca — the westernmost point of mainland Europe — is fifteen minutes north, Cascais ten minutes east, and Sintra over the hill. The seafood restaurants along this beach road are the reason people drive out from Lisbon.

PT0218.tagline: A Colares coastal house with a private tennis court and beach access
PT0218.description:
Casa do Moinho is on the Avenida Alfredo Coelho at Colares, on the Sintra coast, with a private tennis court, beach access and ocean views. Seven bedrooms and seventeen guests make it the largest house in the Lisbon group.

Beyond the tennis court there is a gym, a games room with billiards, a private pool, an indoor fireplace and two workspaces. The scale and the facilities together make it a house for a group that intends to stay put — a reunion, a retreat, a wedding party.

Colares sits between the Sintra hills and the Atlantic, in a wine region small enough that most people have never heard of it and old enough to predate the phylloxera. Praia das Maçãs and Praia Grande are minutes away, the Sintra palaces are ten minutes inland, and Lisbon is under an hour.

PT0031.tagline: A three-bedroom house with a heated pool, a short drive from central Lisbon
PT0031.description:
Casa do Presidente sits on the Estrada do Penedo outside Lisbon, which buys a garden and a heated private pool at a distance from the city that most Lisbon rentals cannot offer. Three bedrooms, eight guests.

The house is arranged for people who intend to spend their days out and their evenings in: an indoor fireplace, a BBQ grill, and a pool that is heated for the shoulder seasons when Lisbon is at its best.

The city is close enough for museums, Alfama, the Gulbenkian and dinner in Príncipe Real, and far enough that you sleep in quiet. Sintra is a short drive west, the Cascais coast a little further. The two-night minimum makes it one of the few houses here that works for a weekend.

PT0061.tagline: A contemporary loft in Marvila, with a private pool in the city
PT0061.description:
Loft 58 is on the Rua Capitão Leitão in Marvila, east Lisbon — the old warehouse district that has become the city's most interesting quarter without losing its industrial shape. Five bedrooms, ten guests, and, unusually for Lisbon, a private outdoor pool.

The architecture is loft-scale: high volumes, open plan, an indoor fireplace, and enough separate bedrooms that ten people are not living on top of each other. A two-night minimum makes it workable for a short city stay.

Marvila is where Lisbon's craft breweries, galleries and the newer restaurants have settled, along the river east of Santa Apolónia. The centre is fifteen minutes by taxi or a straight run on the metro, and the Parque das Nações waterfront is close. For a group who want the city itself rather than a base outside it, a private pool in Lisbon is close to unheard of.
